entries.claim: The Latin text in this revision of Divinum Officium is used for comparison with the printed Missal.

locator.section: In vigilia Ascensionis; Postcommunio; Tribue nobis, Domine

entries.claim: In the Ascension Vigil, the page prints Tribue nobis, Domine through et desiderata percipere (w001–w015), followed by the Per Dominum cue. The full common conclusion (w016–w036) and separate Amen (w037) retain their distinct wording and ritual-boundary sources.

locator.section: Rubricae generales Missalis romani, nn. 505, 511 i, 513 a, 514.

entries.claim: The celebrant says or sings the postcommunion and its conclusion.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 a: Father-directed common conclusion

entries.claim: Rubricae generales 115 a prints the full twenty-one-word Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filium tuum conclusion through per omnia saecula saeculorum and following Amen. It supports the supplied wording at w016–w036 and the separate w037 Amen after the proper page’s Per Dominum cue. Reader accents, ligatures, colon after tuum and uppercase Qui are declared editorial accidentals, not exact typography from this rubric. This use does not assign the response performer or prayer voice.

The cited page prints this prayer’s proper body and the abbreviated conclusion “Per Dóminum”. The full common conclusion and Amen are supplied separately in the reader, with its own accentuation, capitalization and punctuation.
